report.tagline: Block's US money app that started with sending cash to friends and now works like a bank for people who are poorly served by banks, with a debit card, paycheck deposit, short loans, stocks and Bitcoin.
report.simpleSummary: Cash App lets you send money to anyone using a $cashtag, like $alex. Many users get their paycheck into it, spend with a free Cash App Card, and borrow small amounts like $300 until payday. You can also buy stocks and Bitcoin from $1. It earns money from card swipes, instant cash-outs, small loans, Bitcoin sales and buy now, pay later through Afterpay.

overview.whatItDoes: Cash App is a US money app with person-to-person payments, a debit card, direct deposit, savings, small loans (Borrow), buy now pay later (Afterpay), stock and Bitcoin investing and tax filing. It aims at people earning under about $150,000, many of whom do not trust or cannot easily use big banks. Block, the company behind Square, owns it.
howItWorks: You sign up with a phone or email and pick a $cashtag.
You send money to friends for free and receive money into your balance.
You order a free Cash App Card (a Visa debit card) to spend the balance anywhere.
You can move your paycheck to Cash App and get paid up to two days early.
Cash App Borrow offers short loans, and Afterpay lets you split purchases into four payments.
Buy stocks or Bitcoin from $1; cash out to a bank for free in days or instantly for a fee.
overview.valueProposition: For users: a low-fee bank-like app that is easy to open, with early pay, small loans and investing. For Block: a big base of everyday users whose paychecks and spending flow through the app, which it can earn from many times.

businessModel.summary: Cash App earns from many small fees across the money life of a user: card swipes, instant cash-outs, loans, buy now pay later, Bitcoin and interest on balances. Q3 2026 gross profit was $2.07 billion.

revenueStreams.detail: Fees merchants pay when users spend with the Cash App Card.
About 0.5% to 1.75% to move money to a bank right away.
Loan fees and merchant fees; $19 billion of loans in Q3 2026.
$1.77 billion revenue in Q3 2026 but only about $52 million gross profit.
Interest on balances and fees from business users.

businessModel.pricing: Sending money and standard deposits: free. Instant deposit: about 0.5% to 1.75% (min $0.25). Cash App Card: free. ATM: free with $300 or more in direct deposits a month, otherwise $2.50. Borrow: flat fee per loan, shown before accepting.
costDrivers: Loan and fraud losses ($602 million across Block in Q3 2026)
Card processing and bank partner costs
businessModel.unitEconomics: Cash App makes about $34 of gross profit per active user each quarter, roughly $140 a year (our calculation from $2.07 billion and 60 million actives). A user who only sends money to friends earns little. A primary banking user who gets a $2,000 paycheck every two weeks, swipes the card for $1,000 a month and takes a $300 loan earns Cash App several hundred dollars a year from interchange, loan fees and instant deposits. So the plan is to move users to direct deposit, where value per user is many times higher.

howTheyGetUsers: Network effect from friends sending money
Cash App Card designs and Boosts popular with young people
Payroll partnerships with Workday and UKG for direct deposit
Spanish-language app to reach Hispanic users
whatBringsUsersBack: Borrow and Afterpay limits that grow with use
growth.moat: Cash App's moat is its network effect plus data. 60 million monthly users pay each other, and Block sees their paychecks and spending, which helps it price small loans better than banks.

guardrailMetrics: Loan loss rate on Borrow and Afterpay
strengths: Large network of 60 million monthly users
Rich data on income and spending helps lending
weaknesses: History of fraud and scam issues
Bitcoin revenue is large but low margin
Lending to low-income users raises credit risk
risks: CFPB and state regulators on fraud handling and lending
Competition from Chime, Venmo and banks
userComplaints: Scams and payments that cannot be reversed
Accounts closed or frozen without clear reasons

improvementIdeas.idea: Scam warning when paying a new $cashtag with no shared contacts
Clear account review status with a timeline and phone callback
Bigger Borrow limits for users with three months of on-time repayment and direct deposit
improvementIdeas.problem: $300 average limit is too low for real emergencies.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More loan use and direct deposits.

improvementIdeas.idea: Savings goals that auto-save part of each paycheck
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Average balance per primary banking active

pmLessons: A free peer payment feature can become the door to a full bank.
The users who bring the most value are those who make you their main account, so measure them.
Lending to underserved users can be good business, but only with strong risk controls.
Big revenue is not the same as big profit: Bitcoin is huge in sales but small in profit.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you get more Cash App users to set up direct deposit?
interviewQuestions.hint: Funnel from active to deposit; reduce friction with payroll partners; offer early pay and perks.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Cash App raise Borrow limits?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh user need against loss rate; test on safe segments; set guardrails.

interviewQuestions.question: Compare Cash App with Chime.
interviewQuestions.hint: Users, products, revenue mix, network effect vs pure banking.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Cash App's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Primary banking actives; explain why and the drivers.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce scams on Cash App?
interviewQuestions.hint: Types of scams, friction for risky payments, education, data signals, metrics.
